questions.question: “A detailed written working plan of a proposed study designed to investigate a given problem”. Which of the following best describes the above statement?
questions.correct_answer: A. Research proposal

questions.question: Which of the followings is included in “statement of the problem” in the research proposal?
questions.correct_answer: D. Magnitude of the problem

questions.question: Hospital records show an increase in asthma admissions over the past 3 years. In which section in the research proposal should this sentence be written?
questions.correct_answer: B. Statement of the problem

questions.question: In a study assessing the effect of screen time on sleep quality among adolescents, sleep quality represents the which of the following?
questions.correct_answer: C. Dependent variable

questions.question: Which statement best explains the purpose of a pilot study?
questions.correct_answer: B. To test feasibility and data collection tools
wrong_answers: D. To get a conclusion for the research

questions.question: Operationalization of study variables should be provided in the research proposal. What is meant by operationalization?
questions.correct_answer: B. Make them measurable

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the entire group of people (or objects) you wish to generalize the study findings to?
questions.correct_answer: B. Target population

questions.question: Which feature is essential for valid informed consent?
questions.correct_answer: C. Clear explanation in simple language
wrong_answers: D. Signing the form after data collection

questions.question: A participant withdraws from a study after completing the questionnaire. What is the most ethical action?
questions.correct_answer: C. Respect withdrawal and remove data if requested

questions.question: A researcher copies large sections of a previous thesis written by themselves into a new article without citation. This is an example of:
questions.correct_answer: C. Self-plagiarism

questions.question: While writing a proposal, a student summarizes previous studies in their own words and cites the sources correctly. This practice was done to avoid which of the following misconducts?
questions.correct_answer: B Plagiarism

questions.question: Which of the following should be included in the methods section of the research proposal?
questions.correct_answer: D. Ethical considerations
wrong_answers: C. A copy of data collection tool

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the principle of non maleficence?
questions.correct_answer: C. Avoiding actions that may cause harm
wrong_answers: A. Providing financial compensation to all participants
B. Ensuring the researcher receives recognition
D. Ensuring equal access to benefits of research

questions.question: The ethical principle of beneficence requires that researchers:
questions.correct_answer: C. Maximize possible benefits of the research
wrong_answers: A. Protect only those who request it
B. Avoid disclosing the research purpose

questions.question: Which scenario reflects a failure of non-maleficence?
questions.correct_answer: C. Administering a painful procedure without clear medical benefit
wrong_answers: A. Not informing the participant of their rights
B. Failing to publish the research
D. Offering too much money to influence participation

questions.question: Which scenario best demonstrates respect for autonomy?
questions.correct_answer: B. Allowing participants to withdraw from a study at any time
wrong_answers: A. Including participants without informing them of the risks
C. Encouraging participants to stay in the study for better results
D. Selecting participants based on convenience

questions.question: The ethical principle of justice in research primarily focuses on:
questions.correct_answer: B. Fair distribution of research benefits and burdens

questions.question: When must informed consent be obtained in a research study?
questions.correct_answer: B. Before conducting any study-related activities
wrong_answers: C. Only if the participant requests it

questions.question: Informed consent ensures that a participant:
questions.correct_answer: B. Understands and voluntarily agrees to participate
wrong_answers: A. Must complete the study once started
C. Gives permission without knowing the study's details
D. Signs a form to protect the researchers legally

questions.question: A researcher is computing the infant mortality rate during the year 2025 and wants to obtain the total number of live births that represents the denominator. What would be the source of the data?
questions.correct_answer: B. Vital statistics

questions.question: “An outbreak of acute watery diarrhea occurred”. Which health information platform provides a legal framework for physicians for the timely reporting of cases to the public health authorities?
questions.correct_answer: C. System for notifiable infectious diseases
wrong_answers: B. Hospital records used for patients' care
D. Sentinel surveillance system of diseases

questions.question: “An oncologist is studying the five-year survival rate of breast cancer patients in Egypt”. What is the specific source of data to track this information?
questions.correct_answer: B. Population-based disease registries
wrong_answers: D. National system of death registration

questions.question: “A public health researcher observed that smoking habit is missing for most of the patient attending the Main University Hospital”. Which approach is the most appropriate to obtain data on smoking habits of the population served by this hospital?
questions.correct_answer: B. Conduct health and morbidity survey
wrong_answers: A. Review the recent population census
C. Obtain the per-capita cigarette sales
D. Contact patients to complete the data

questions.question: “A Ministry of Health official is evaluating the efficiency of family health centers by analyzing the number of daily admissions and patient outcomes”. Under which category does this information fall?
questions.correct_answer: B. Health service records

questions.question: Which term refers to the “approach of information gathering”?
questions.correct_answer: B. Method of data collection

questions.question: “A researcher decided to use the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) database to study trends in maternal health". What is the primary limitation expected from the data?
questions.correct_answer: B. Tailoring the research aims to the available variables.
wrong_answers: A. Retrieving the relevant variables is time consuming
C. Acquiring specific skills for the extraction of the data
D. Representation of mothers attending health facilities

questions.question: Which source of data represents a secondary source of nutrition assessment of children below 5 years?
questions.correct_answer: B. Weight and height recorded in nurseries annually
wrong_answers: A. Trend of malnutrition published in scientific articles
C. Daily dietary intake completed by the mother
D. Deaths of children below the age of 5-years

questions.question: “A scientist justifies the use of secondary data from population census rather than primary data”. What is the most likely Justification for the use of secondary data?
questions.correct_answer: B. It is less costly and more resource saving
wrong_answers: A. It is complete and relevant to die aims
C. It is free from recall and interviewers’ bias
D. It is easier in the application of statistical tests

questions.question: Which research aim is consistent with conducting a “health and morbidity surveys”?
questions.correct_answer: A. To obtain a representative estimate of a health problem
wrong_answers: B. To ensure the mandatory reporting of infectious diseases
C. To monitor the outcomes of an epidemic or an outbreak
D. To evaluate the post-marketing efficiency of a treatment

questions.question: “A researcher is collecting data on the behavior pattern of children by interviewing their parents”. What is the expected limitation?
questions.correct_answer: B.  Socially desired responses
wrong_answers: C. High cost of data collection

questions.question: “Research aims at identifying shared views and community attitudes related to the traditional healing practices in a rural community”. What is the most suitable method for the collection of relevant data?
questions.correct_answer: B. Focus group discussion

questions.question: What is the purpose of using “probes” in an in-depth interview?
questions.correct_answer: B. To further explore participants’ response
wrong_answers: A. To guide participants to a specific answer
C. To standardize response across participants
D. To shorten the duration of the interview

questions.question: What is the purpose of “audio recording” and taking “field notes” during a focus group discussion on child feeding practices?
questions.correct_answer: B. To capture contextual details that might be otherwise overlooked
wrong_answers: A. To quantify participants responses for analysis and reporting
C. To replace the need for a facilitator during and after the discussion
D. To engage participants and maintain their interest in the discussion

questions.question: An observer noticed that nurses are more adherent to hand-hygiene protocols when they are aware that they are watched. Which term refers to this phenomenon?
questions.correct_answer: C. Hawthorne effect

questions.question: Which measure is taken to minimize "observer's bias" while recording surgical performance using a checklist?
questions.correct_answer: C. Training the observer on the intended task
wrong_answers: A. Shortening the period of observation
B. Increasing the number of procedures to be observed
D. Recording the observation at the end of the procedure

questions.question: A researcher intends to collect data on the prevalence of smoking in a factory of 2000 workers. What would be the most suitable method of data collection?
questions.correct_answer: C. Interview questionnaire

questions.question: A question reading “Do you agree that childhood vaccines are safe and effective? ” has been rejected for not meeting the required standard. What is the likely reason?
questions.correct_answer: B. It is double-barreled
wrong_answers: D. It suggests a favorable answer

questions.question: Which question inquiring into the intake of sugar meets the recommended wording and structure?
questions.correct_answer: C. Do you use more than 2 spoons of sugar daily? "
wrong_answers: A. "Do you frequently consume sugary snacks? "
B. "Do you take a lot of sugar in your daily diet? "
D. "Do you have a regular habit of taking sugar? "

questions.question: A researcher determined the information that should be collected from participants using a questionnaire. What is the next step in developing the questionnaire?
questions.correct_answer: B. Decide on the necessity of each question
wrong_answers: A. Pre-test the questionnaire on a purposive sample
C. Organize the questions in a meaningful order
D. Specify the type and form of the question

questions.question: “Research on domestic violence includes 5 questions inquiring into sensitive issues”. Where should the researcher place these questions while organizing the final version of the questionnaire?
questions.correct_answer: C. Near the end of the core questions after the establishing of rapport
wrong_answers: A. At the beginning to alert participants to the focus of the study
B. After the demographic section in case participants decided to withdraw
D. Scattered throughout the questionnaire to distract participants

questions.question: What is the primary objective of ’’pre-testing” the final draft a questionnaire on a small sample of respondents?
questions.correct_answer: B. To identify ambiguous questions or terms that are difficult for respondent
wrong_answers: A. TO gather the preliminary data needed to finalize the research proposal
C. To decide on demographic groups that should be excluded from the study
D. To train data collectors on asking questions and recording the responses

questions.question: In which situation is an anonymous self-administered questionnaire preferred over face-to-face interview?
questions.correct_answer: C. Collecting data on the use of illicit drugs among high school students
wrong_answers: A. Collecting clinical data from patients admitted to private hospitals
B. Collecting data on psychological status of children with hearing defects
D. Collecting data on lifestyle among old people living in elderly homes

questions.question: What is specific to a “test e.g, psychometric tests” compared to a “questionnaire” to assess personality disorder?
questions.correct_answer: A. It is a standardised tool
wrong_answers: B. It is based on self-report

questions.question: What is the best place of the set of questions inquiring into the demographic characteristics of participants in a questionnaire?
questions.correct_answer: C. At the end of the questionnaire
wrong_answers: A. At the beginning of the questionnaire
B. in the middle with the core questions
